What I did:
- I made my own copy of the current apps/lab (the same sheet as the research build: styles-DdB1bnNp.css, 429,987 bytes) and 10 variants.
- I wrote new scripts (check/*.mjs) and ran each key measurement again in turns, 5 runs, at a load average of 3 to 65 on 14 cores.
- The two runs that give the times of the part had a load average of 2.8 to 11.8. This is lower than the research runs (4 to 223). It is not a quiet machine.

Main results:
- The three causes of the research agent hold: the hover glider of a nav, the `:has()` rule shape, and the sibling rule shape. The count follows the three sibling rules when I remove them and put them back in one page (2,435, then 83, then 2,435, then 83).
- Four findings change the draft:
  1. The sibling cost is only for an element that is added or removed before a sibling. An element that is added as the last child costs nothing.
  2. With each folder open, only 8 of the first 60 arrow keys recalculate the document. The other 52 recalculate 15 to 67 elements.
  3. The style cost for each element is on the elements with `ak-layer`: about 170 µs each, against 2 µs for an element with no class.
  4. The direction document of the lab has hover and focus gliders in each list. So "bar glider only" removes two gliders of the picked direction, and is not only "what the note asked for".
- The record gets 1 part (826 words of prose, 2 tables, 1 demo, 3 decision panels at their evidence), 10 findings (PERF-01 to PERF-10), 1 change of PRIM-17, 3 proposed decisions, 2 prose patches, 14 listed count statements, and 2 terms.

verdict: Confirmed with corrections. The causes, the two rewrites, and the direction and rough size of each timing are reproduced. 18 claims of the draft were wrong, too wide, or not exact, and they are corrected in the repaired files. One research timing was not reproduced (rows in parts at 41 rows: 34 ms against 32 ms, not 35 against 48), so it is no longer a fact of the part. No proposal settles a decision.
directAnswer:
The size of the generated file is not the cause. Chrome parses the sheet in 5 to 13 ms (measured by the earlier lanes, not again here).

The work that the rules give to Chrome is the cause. It is in the primitive layer, in three places:

1. `ak-layer` of @ariakit/tailwind (output.css:118). Measured: one element with `ak-layer` costs about 170 µs at a full recalculation when Chrome cannot reuse a computed style. An element with no class costs 2 µs. The review page has 522 such elements in 1,731, and one full recalculation costs 84 ms. The 51 typed `@property` rules are not the cost: without a type, colors are 15 times slower.

2. The hover glider of a nav (packages/ariakit-ui/src/styles/nav.ts:381 and :385 at ariakit/ariakit commit 643a23af). Measured: one arrow key recalculates 1,217 of 1,734 elements. With the bar glider only: 70.

```ts
// As built: the nav is the anchor of a :has() outside the subject.
"[.nav:not(:has(:is(li>.control,.nav>.control):hover))>&]:hidden",
// Tested in a copy of the lab only: 72 elements, equal pictures.
"[&:not(:has(~.control:hover,~*_li>.control:hover))]:hidden",
```

3. Two rule shapes. The `:has()` shape (10 class names of choice.ts, control.ts, input.ts) lets each `:has()` anchor recalculate its subtree. The sibling shape (glider.ts:129, glider.ts:138, tabs.ts:381) makes Chrome recalculate the subtree of a parent when a child is added or removed before a sibling. Ariakit removes the portal node of a tooltip from `<body>`, so that key recalculates the document: 2,435 of 2,589 elements.

The lab did one thing without need for speed: 10 live frames in the gallery (3,185 requests and 3.8 to 5.1 s on a development server, against 223 requests and 0.9 to 1.1 s with the frame documents blocked). The four gliders of the list are not a lab mistake: the direction document has hover and focus gliders in each list.

The real app will not be slow as the lab is. It is one document, and its list has the bar glider only (apps/web/src/review/item-list.tsx:307). Two things are in its copy today (counted, not measured there): the three sibling rules are in its built sheet, and the two hover rules are at nav.ariakit.react.tsx:299 and :303.

For the settled review page, at 41 rows and a load average of 3 to 12:
- Arrow key: 80 ms as built, 36 ms with the bar glider only (344 ms and 134 ms with the CPU slowed 4 times).
- Approve stays near 200 ms with the CPU slowed 4 times in each form with no hover glider cost (196 to 218 ms). Script is then the larger part: 33 ms of script against 24 ms of style and layout for one arrow key.

No time is the time of a quiet machine. The counts are stable.

fullDocumentInvalidation:
Confirmed, with one correction of the trigger and one of the size.

**The rules (Ariakit UI style layer).** Three class names, each alone enough:
- `styles/glider.ts:129`: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:outline-none`
- `styles/glider.ts:138`: `not-ui-sibling-selected:hidden`
- `styles/tabs.ts:381`: `not-peer-ui-focus-visible:invisible`

```css
.not-peer-ui-focus-visible\:outline-none:not(:is(:where(.peer):is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) ~ *))
```

**The rule put back and removed (measured, check/body.mjs, 585 rows, 5 rounds in one page each):**
- As built: 2,435 elements in the largest recalculation.
- One rule removed (each of the three): 2,435.
- Two rules removed (each pair): 2,435.
- The three removed: 83.
- The three put back: 2,435. Removed again: 83.
- With the built sheet of the rewrite: 83 in each state.

**The trigger, corrected (measured, check/direct.mjs, no React).** One empty hidden div, 41 rows, bar form:

| Place of the div | As built | Three rules removed | With the rewrite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<body>`, last child | 94 | 94 | 94 |
| `<body>`, before the last child | 1,637 | 96 | 96 |
| `<body>`, first child | 1,637 | 69 | 67 |

So the cost is for an element that is added or removed before a sibling. It is the same at 41 rows as at 585 rows (2,488 of 2,494). Ariakit appends a portal node and removes it from the middle of the children of `<body>`.

**The size, corrected (measured, check/pager-walk.mjs).** `VariantPager` (apps/lab/src/explorations/kits/ariakit/variants/pager.tsx:61, `<Hint key={variant.key}>`) removes and adds 3 tooltips only when the variant keys of the next screenshot differ. In 60 arrow keys with each folder open: 8 keys change the children of `<body>` (2,433 to 2,457 elements, 335 ms); 52 keys do not (15 to 67 elements, 110 ms). At 41 rows no key changes them.

**The rewrite (tested in a copy of the lab only):**

```css
/* styles/ui.css:1063. As built: &:is(:focus-visible, [data-focus-visible]) */
@custom-variant ui-focus-visible {
  &:focus-visible,
  &[data-focus-visible] { @slot; }
}
/* styles/ui.css:1256, ui-sibling-selected: the list at the left of ~ starts with */
:is(:checked:where(.control), [aria-checked="true"], ...) ~ &,
```

- Counted (check/css-diff.mjs): 2,878 rules in both sheets, 63 selectors change, no declaration changes, 429,987 to 436,633 bytes.
- Measured: 85 elements and 136 ms for the 8 keys, not 2,435 and 335 ms. Pictures: 0 pixels differ in each state, both views, both themes.
- Not tested: apps/web, the tests of Ariakit. The second branch of `ui-sibling-selected` (`&:has(~ :is(:checked, ...))`) keeps `:checked` with no class, so the two branches are no longer symmetric.

**Ownership (counted).** Tailwind CSS 4.3.3 writes the `~ *` (node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/lib.mjs, the `peer` variant: `` v.selector = `&:is(${k} ~ *)` ``). The alternative with no class comes from the custom variants of Ariakit UI. The built sheet of apps/web (apps/web/dist/client/assets/index-CXm4JU5N.css) has the three rules.

**A second effect that is not this cause (measured, new).** One element added to the main panel recalculates 1,546 of 1,636 elements, with and without the three sibling rules. DevTools names the Shell root (`div.shell`) and the 11 selectors of the `:has()` rule shape (check/why.mjs). With the 10 class names removed: 124. So the `:has()` shape has two measured anchors: the nav with a hover glider, and the Shell root.

**Not run again:** the 26 synthetic rules of the research agent (which shapes are slow) and the DevTools event on `BODY`. I read the logs. The mechanism inside Chrome stays an assumption: nobody read its source.
typedProperties:
The result of the research agent holds: no faster form with an equal picture exists among the registrations. I add where the cost is.

**Measured (check/props.mjs, 5 rounds of 4 theme switches in turns, load average 6 to 9; pictures by check/props-pics.mjs with a full-sheet picture before each variant, noise 0 to 10 pixels of 1,296,000):**

| Variant | µs for each element | Against full | Pixels that differ (dark, light) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full sheet | 52 [50-65] | 1 | noise |
| The 51 typed rules removed | 18 | 0.35 | 1,080,060 and 1,010,896 (broken) |
| `syntax: "*"` on the 26 numbers | 54.6 | 1.05 | 0 and 8 (equal) |
| `syntax: "*"` on the 14 colors | 786 | 15 | 35,357 and 22,821 |
| `syntax: "*"` on the 11 lengths | 309 | 5.9 | 5,969 and 5,916 |
| `inherits: true` on the 32 with `false` | 53.4 | 1.03 | 42,493 and 43,908 (not equal) |

Research numbers at a load average of 70 to 77: 57.2, 17.9, 14 times, 6.7 times, 8% more. Same direction and size.

**What else reads the 51 properties (counted in node_modules/@ariakit/tailwind/src/output.css, version 0.2.8):**
- 371 style queries; 330 read a typed property: `--_ak-ltlc-even` 132, `--_ak-ltlc-odd` 132, `--_ak-ltl` 34, `--_ak-ll` 19, `--_ak-lbd` 4, `--_ak-ls` 2 (6 colors), `--_ak-frame-row` 4 (number), `--ak-frame-padding` 3 (length). A style query compares the computed value, so these 8 need their type.

```css
/* output.css:77 */
@custom-variant ak-dark {
  @container style(--_ak-ls: oklch(1 0 0)) { @slot; }
}
```

- No transition and no animation is in the package. The transitions of the primitives (disclosure.ts:223, progress.ts:123, shell.ts:527, tabs.ts:391, ui.css:1486) read other properties.
- The 51 typed rules are at lines 1547 to 2251. `ak-layer` is at lines 118 to 166.

**Where the cost is (measured, new, check/util-cost.mjs --unique 1, load average about 40).** 1,000 elements added to the page, each alone in a parent div and with its own inline custom property:
- No class: 4.6 µs for a pair (about 2 µs for one element).
- `ak-layer`: 176 µs for a pair (about 170 µs for the element).
- The most frequent class set of the page (`ak-layer ak-layer-transparent ak-frame ...`, 245 uses): 191 µs.
- Text class sets with `ak-ink-70`: 22 to 30 µs.

Estimate: 522 elements with `ak-layer` at 170 µs are 89 ms, the size of one full recalculation of the page (84 ms).

A first form of this run had 1,000 equal siblings: 1.6 µs for `ak-layer`. Chrome reuses one computed style for equal siblings. That run is not the cost of the formulas, and it is not in the part.

**Actionable for @ariakit/tailwind:** the cost is the formulas that `ak-layer` writes (7 relative colors in a chain and 4 more), on each element that has the class and cannot share a style. Fewer elements with `ak-layer`, or fewer formulas in it, is where a gain can be. Not tested: which formula costs how much, and a form of `ak-layer` with fewer formulas. The research test \"no `ak-layer` on 304 transparent layers: 10% less, 3% to 5% of pixels differ\" was not run again.

proposedDecisions.question: Which gliders does the screenshot list of the review page have?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) four-as-built: keep the four gliders. Arrow key 80 ms, 344 ms with the CPU slowed 4 times; Approve 425 ms at 4x; pointer 483 ms; wheel 817 ms. The minimal option. (b) bar-only: 36 ms, 134 ms at 4x; Approve 218 ms at 4x; pointer 24 ms; wheel 60 ms; 70 elements, not 1,217. Pictures equal in 5 of 6 states at 41 rows. Only the bar travels; in a folder the focus ring is 3 px inside; the hover and focus gliders of the direction document go. One prop, no primitive change (agrees with D-UI-02 and the lab note). (c) all-but-hover: selected, focus, and bar gliders. 36 ms, 151 ms at 4x; 72 elements; pictures equal in 7 of 8 states with folders; the hover glider of the direction document goes. (d) four-after-ariakit: four gliders after rewrite 1 in Ariakit UI and a refresh of the copy (agrees with D-UI-02: the copy stays unmodified). 37 ms, 160 ms at 4x; 72 elements; pictures equal; pointer 265 ms and wheel 277 ms stay (1,499 ms for the wheel at 585 rows); waits for another repository. Removed: "the row draws the bar" (no bar in a folder, hand-placed code, against the lab note).
proposedDecisions.recommended: bar-only. It is the simplest form, and it has the lowest cost for the pointer and the wheel. Measured: 70 recalculated elements against 1,217, and 24 ms against 483 ms for the pointer. It is a recommendation, not a settled answer.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The maintainer wants the hover and focus gliders of the direction document in this list. Then four-after-ariakit keeps the look, and all-but-hover keeps the focus ring and the selected surface. Only Chrome was measured, which is the scope of D-RES-04.

proposedDecisions.question: Does apps/web get a test for the speed of the review page when the settled design goes in?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) no-test: the minimal option. No work. A hover glider on a long list, or a refresh of the primitives with a new rule of the two shapes, can bring the cost back with no signal. (b) count-test: one browser test turns the size containers off, presses ArrowDown and A, and fails when the largest style recalculation is above a limit. Lab numbers: 1,217 and 1,345 as built; 70 and 156 with the bar glider only; 2,435 against 85 for a key that removes tooltips. The test changes the page: with size containers Chrome reports 37 elements for each form. The numbers of apps/web are not known. It does not limit script. (c) time-test: fails above 200 ms with the CPU slowed 4 times. The same build gave 134 ms at a load average of 3 to 12 and 184 to 232 ms at 33 to 44. Approve is at the limit in each form (196 to 218 ms).
proposedDecisions.recommended: count-test. Measured: the count was equal in each of 10 runs at a load average of 3 to 12 and in the research runs at 4 to 78; the time changed by a factor of 1.4 to 2 with the load. It is a recommendation, not a settled answer.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The maintainer puts the test in Ariakit UI, where the two rule shapes are: then no test in apps/web is the simpler choice. Or a test that turns the size containers off is not acceptable.

proposedDecisions.question: Does the gallery of the lab show pictures in place of live frames?
proposedDecisions.options: (a) keep-live-frames: the minimal option. No work. Each load of the gallery costs 3 to 4 s more on a development server and 14 times the requests (3,185 against 223). The first load after a server start needed 9.2 s, and one load did not get a quiet network in 30 s at a load average of about 58. (b) pictures: pictures in the gallery and the directions page, live frames in the two explorers. Quiet after 0.9 to 1.1 s on a development server (the measurement with the frame documents blocked; nobody built the pictures). A card no longer follows the theme and the look controls. The pictures need a capture step.
proposedDecisions.recommended: pictures. Measured on the lab of today (10 frames): 3.8 to 5.1 s against 0.9 to 1.1 s on a development server. It is a recommendation, not a settled answer. This choice changes the temporary lab only; no settled decision of the record depends on it.
proposedDecisions.wrongIf: The maintainer no longer opens the gallery. The design is settled and the lab is temporary, so no work is then the simpler choice.
